title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Qu\'ebec French
abstract: arXiv:2611.24699v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture its effects. In this paper, we present a controlled study of CPT for Qu\'ebec French language understanding across nine LLMs spanning different families and scales. Using a budget-matched protocol of 30M tokens per experiment, our results show that the benefit of CPT depends strongly on the starting model's existing competence in the target variety. When CPT is beneficial, the improvements are driven more by corpus composition than by data volume, with literary text accounting for most of the gain. translated_title: 持续预训练何时有效？一项关于魁北克法语方言适应的对照研究
translated_abstract: 持续预训练（CPT）被广泛用于将预训练语言模型适配到方言和非标准语言变体，但这种额外的训练何时才是必要的、其收益由什么驱动、以及总体评估分数是否足以刻画其效果，目前仍不清楚。本文针对魁北克法语语言理解任务，对涵盖不同模型家族与规模的九个大语言模型开展了一项持续预训练的对照研究。采用每个实验3000万词元的预算匹配协议，我们的结果表明：持续预训练的收益在很大程度上取决于起始模型对目标语言变体已有的掌握程度。当持续预训练带来收益时，其提升更多源于语料构成而非数据量，其中文学文本贡献了大部分增益。对魁北克法语与标准法语的成对评估进一步表明，持续预训练主要改善的是表达理解能力而非语法能力，并且语料库……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过对九个大语言模型的预算匹配对照实验发现，持续预训练对魁北克法语方言适应的收益取决于起始模型对目标方言的既有能力，其增益主要由语料构成（尤其是文学文本）而非数据量驱动，且主要提升表达理解而非语法能力。
en_tdlr: Through budget-matched controlled experiments on nine LLMs, this study shows that continual pre-training's benefits for Québec French adaptation depend on the starting model's existing competence in the target dialect, are driven mainly by corpus composition (especially literary text) rather than data volume, and primarily improve expression comprehension rather than grammatical competence.
